TEACHER REFERENCE

Checkpoint must-haves

    TOPIC 2.3 · CHECKPOINT 1

    What counts as evidence?

    Criteria are for this response only. They do not describe a student’s general ability. Source: College Board CED, effective Fall 2026, Topic 2.3, pp. 57–58.

    FROM PATTERN TO NEXT STEP

    Read the writing before deciding

    A colored segment is a provisional interpretation of one response. Read the full response and highlighted evidence, check the criterion, and correct a judgment when you disagree.

    Partly shown can mean an incomplete explanation. Not yet shown can mean a missing causal connection or a misconception. The written interpretation helps distinguish these; the color alone cannot.

    Needs review, not analyzed, blank, and missing work remain separate. None of these establishes a learning gap. Choose a focused next step only after checking the supporting responses.

    A documented teaching decision shows use of the tool. It does not demonstrate improved student learning.
